text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- European market boosts food and detergent giant Unilever Q2 net by 57 percent to Dfl 1,477 million. (p1)
- KLM/Royal Dutch Airlines talking for year and a half with Alitalia, according to interview with departing KLM board chairman Pieter Bouw. (p1)
- Northern Netherlands' development agency NOM subsidy helped to lure Japanese soy sauce producer Kikkoman. (p1)
- Philips Electronics upgrades Brussels office, aimed at lobbying European Union officials. (p3)
- Dutch transporters expect slight improvement in profitability, according to branch organisation TLN economic research. (p3)
VOLKSKRANT
- Internet provider NLnet offers 500 businesses and private customers telecomunications via internet as experiment this month. (p2)
- Turnover of medicines will grow by one billion guilders until year 2000, according to Distrifood magazine. (p2)
- Public prosecutor mulls prosecution of chemicals firm Vos for shipping poisoned glycerin from which 60 children died on Haiti in 1995. (p3)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Charter companies perplexed by permission for Royal Air Maroc's night flights over Schiphol airport. (p3)
- GIM capital management launches investment fund for small investors. (p11)
- Accord between KLM and U.S. partner Northwest Airlines will cost some 1,300 jobs. (p1)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- De Unie, union for industry and services sector, will demand 3.5 pct higher wages in next pay and conditions talks. (p9)
- Chemical giant Akzo Nobel looking for partners for fibre division. (p9) -
TROUW
- New political movement seeking greater autonomy for the three northern provinces of the Netherlands. (p3) A-
